Claude Code Prompt — Nightly RAG Corpus Agent (v1, Queue + Starter List)
Build from: `/c/Users/kjemery/Arete/Arete/`
Run with: `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, Sonnet specified
Windows/PowerShell constraints: no `&&` chaining, no `echo ""` file creation, no EAS build commands, no web/ directory changes
Overview
Build the first autonomous agent from the Arete AI Agent System spec: the RAG Corpus Agent. This is a scheduled nightly job on Railway that grows the RAG corpus without human intervention, working through a hardcoded starter list of public-domain texts first, then an ongoing Supabase queue that Kyle can add to anytime.
Critical constraint — reuse, don't rebuild. The ingestion pipeline already exists at `academy/corpus-ingestion/` (`ingest.js`, `chunker.js`, `embedder.js`, `uploader.js`). It chunks at 400 words / 50-word overlap, embeds via OpenAI `text-embedding-3-small`, and writes to the `rag_corpus` table (retrieved via the `match_rag_corpus` RPC). This agent WRAPS that pipeline in a scheduler and a source queue. Do NOT rewrite the chunking, embedding, or upload logic.
Scope discipline:

* This v1 does NOT include AI gap analysis, AI source discovery, or AI quality scoring. Those are later phases. This is reliable scheduled ingestion of a human-approved queue, plus a coverage report. Nothing more.
* The dead table `source_text_chunks` must never be written to. Confirm the live pipeline writes to `rag_corpus`.
Commit each part separately. Do NOT push until all parts are clean.
Part 0 — Inspect the Existing Pipeline First
Before writing anything, read and report:

1. `academy/corpus-ingestion/ingest.js` — how it's invoked (CLI args), what it expects as input (file path? manifest? text directory?)
2. `academy/corpus-ingestion/chunker.js` — the chunking entry function signature
3. `academy/corpus-ingestion/embedder.js` — the embed function signature
4. `academy/corpus-ingestion/uploader.js` — confirm it writes to `rag_corpus`, and report the exact column names it expects (e.g. `content`, `embedding`, `source_title`, `author`, `work`, `chunk_index`, `course_relevance`, `difficulty`, etc.)
5. How `.env` is loaded in that directory and which vars it needs (`SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`)
Report all of this before proceeding. The rest of this prompt assumes the agent calls the existing pipeline functions — adjust the integration to match what you actually find.
Part 1 — Supabase Migration: Source Queue + Run Log
Apply via Supabase MCP (project ref: `zhaarabzemhantyxxckq`). Do NOT add to application startup.

```sql
-- Queue of sources to ingest
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS corpus_ingestion_queue (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  source_url TEXT,                    -- URL to fetch (Gutenberg, PerseusDL raw, etc.)
  author TEXT NOT NULL,
  work TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- title of the work
  language TEXT DEFAULT 'en',         -- 'en', 'grc' (ancient Greek), 'lat' (Latin)
  course_relevance TEXT,              -- e.g. 'PHIL 701', nullable
  difficulty TEXT,                    -- e.g. 'Introductory', nullable
  source_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'public_domain'
    CHECK (source_type IN ('public_domain', 'original_language', 'summary')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending'
    CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'processing', 'done', 'failed', 'skipped')),
  priority INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 100,  -- lower = higher priority
  notes TEXT,
  error_message TEXT,
  chunks_ingested INT,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  processed_at TIMESTAMPTZ
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_corpus_queue_status_priority
  ON corpus_ingestion_queue(status, priority);

-- Log of each nightly run for the coverage report
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS corpus_ingestion_runs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  run_started_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  run_completed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  sources_processed INT DEFAULT 0,
  sources_succeeded INT DEFAULT 0,
  sources_failed INT DEFAULT 0,
  total_chunks_added INT DEFAULT 0,
  coverage_report JSONB,              -- author -> chunk count snapshot
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running'
    CHECK (status IN ('running', 'completed', 'failed'))
);

-- Both tables are backend-only (service role). Enable RLS with no policies
-- so the anon key cannot touch them; the Railway service role bypasses RLS.
ALTER TABLE corpus_ingestion_queue ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
ALTER TABLE corpus_ingestion_runs ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

```

Report the migration applied successfully and both tables exist.
Commit message: `feat(db): add corpus_ingestion_queue and corpus_ingestion_runs tables`
Part 2 — Seed the Starter List
Create a seed script at `academy/corpus-ingestion/seed-queue.js` that inserts the starter list into `corpus_ingestion_queue` (idempotent — use upsert on `author` + `work`, or check-before-insert, so re-running doesn't duplicate).
The starter list — all public domain, all expand the corpus into new philosophical territory:

```javascript
const STARTER_SOURCES = [
  // --- Eastern philosophy (public domain translations) ---
  { author: 'Confucius', work: 'The Analects', language: 'en',
    source_url: 'https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330.txt',
    source_type: 'public_domain', priority: 10,
    notes: 'Legge translation, 1861. New domain — Eastern virtue ethics.' },
  { author: 'Laozi', work: 'Tao Te Ching', language: 'en',
    source_url: 'https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/216/pg216.txt',
    source_type: 'public_domain', priority: 10,
    notes: 'Legge translation.' },
  { author: 'Sun Tzu', work: 'The Art of War', language: 'en',
    source_url: 'https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/132/pg132.txt',
    source_type: 'public_domain', priority: 20,
    notes: 'Giles translation, 1910. Strategy / leadership domain.' },

  // --- Stoic / classical gaps ---
  { author: 'Michel de Montaigne', work: 'Essays', language: 'en',
    source_url: 'https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3600/pg3600.txt',
    source_type: 'public_domain', priority: 30,
    notes: 'Cotton translation. Already flagged for ingestion in roadmap.' },
```

Important: Gutenberg URLs occasionally change their numeric IDs. The script should fetch each URL and verify it returns plausible text (HTTP 200, body length over a few KB, not an HTML error page) before inserting. If a URL fails verification, insert the row with `status = 'failed'` and an `error_message` noting the bad URL, so Kyle can fix it rather than the source silently vanishing. Report which URLs verified and which didn't.
Note: `archive.ubuntu.com` etc. are allowlisted but `gutenberg.org` may not be reachable from the Claude Code build sandbox. If fetching fails in-sandbox, still insert the rows as `pending` (the actual fetch happens at runtime on Railway, which has open egress) — just note in the report that in-sandbox verification was skipped due to network restrictions.

Part 3 — The Agent: Nightly Ingestion Job
Create `academy/corpus-ingestion/corpus-agent.js`. This is the autonomous job. Logic:

```
1. Create a corpus_ingestion_runs row (status 'running').

2. Pull up to N pending sources from corpus_ingestion_queue,
   ordered by priority ASC, created_at ASC. Default N = 3 per night
   (configurable via env CORPUS_AGENT_BATCH_SIZE). Keeps OpenAI cost
   and run time bounded.

3. For each source:
   a. Mark status 'processing'.
   b. Fetch source_url (use fetch / axios — Railway has open egress).
   c. If it's a Gutenberg text, strip the Gutenberg header/footer
      boilerplate (everextisting between the *** START OF ... *** and
      *** END OF ... *** markers). Add a small helper for this.
   d. If language is 'grc' or 'lat' and the body is XML (PerseusDL),
      strip XML tags to plaintext. (For v1 the starter list is all
      English, so this path can be a simple stub with a TODO — do not
      over-build it.)
   e. Write the cleaned text to a temp file in the format the existing
      pipeline expects (check Part 0 — likely Author_Title_Section_Language.txt
      in a texts/ dir, or a direct file path arg).
   f. Invoke the EXISTING pipeline (ingest.js or its underlying
      chunker+embedder+uploader functions) against that text, passing
      author, work, language, course_relevance, difficulty as metadata.
   g. Count chunks added. Update the queue row: status 'done',
      chunks_ingested, processed_at.
   h. On any error: status 'failed', error_message, processed_at.
      Continue to the next source — one failure never aborts the run.

4. After the batch, build a coverage report: query rag_corpus grouped
   by author, count chunks per author. Store as JSONB on the runs row.

5. Update the runs row: status 'completed', counts, run_completed_at.

6. Print a human-readable summary to stdout (this becomes the morning
   report — Railway logs capture it). Format:

   === Corpus Agent Run [date] ===
   Processed: 3 | Succeeded: 2 | Failed: 1 | Chunks added: 412
   Failed: Sun Tzu / The Art of War — fetch returned 404
   Corpus now: 4,221 chunks across 18 authors
   Thinnest coverage: Cleanthes (12), Musonius Rufus (18), Sun Tzu (0)
   ================================

```

Cost guard: hard cap the batch at `CORPUS_AGENT_BATCH_SIZE` sources AND add a safety ceiling — if a single source would produce more than, say, 5,000 chunks (a very large work like Montaigne's complete Essays), split it across multiple nights by ingesting only the first unprocessed portion and re-queueing the remainder, OR simply log a warning and ingest it fully but note the cost. Pick the simpler option (full ingest + warning) for v1 — just make sure one giant source can't silently rack up a huge embedding bill. Document which you chose.
The agent must be runnable two ways:

* `node corpus-agent.js` — manual run (for testing tonight)
* Invoked by the Railway scheduler (Part 4)
Commit message: `feat(corpus-agent): nightly autonomous ingestion job with coverage report`
Part 4 — Railway Scheduling
Railway runs cron via either a `railway.json`/`railway.toml` cron service or a separate scheduled service. Check how the existing Railway backend is configured (`server/index.js` is the main service — look for `railway.json`, `railway.toml`, `Procfile`, or `nixpacks.toml` in the repo).
Set up the corpus agent to run nightly (suggest 3:00 AM ET = 08:00 UTC). Two viable approaches — pick whichever fits the existing Railway setup:
Option A — Railway cron service (preferred if the project supports it): add a cron schedule entry that runs `node academy/corpus-ingestion/corpus-agent.js` on a `0 8 * * *` schedule.
Option B — node-cron inside an existing or new lightweight process: if Railway cron isn't configured, add `node-cron` and schedule the job. Only do this if it won't interfere with the main `server/index.js` web process — prefer a separate Railway service over bolting a scheduler onto the API server.
Do NOT couple the agent to the main API server's request lifecycle. It should be its own scheduled invocation.
Report exactly how Railway is currently configured and which scheduling approach you used, including the config file changes.
Commit message: `feat(corpus-agent): schedule nightly run on Railway`
Part 5 — A Tiny Manual Add Helper (optional convenience)
Create `academy/corpus-ingestion/queue-add.js` — a one-liner CLI so Kyle can add a source to the queue without writing SQL:

```
node queue-add.js --author "Epictetus" --work "Fragments" --url "https://..." --priority 5

```

It just inserts one `pending` row into `corpus_ingestion_queue`. Keep it minimal.
